newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan TI-Acer issues T$4.25 bln preferred shares.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan TI-Acer issues T$4.25 bln preferred shares.

text.p: Taiwan semiconductor joint venture TI-Acer Inc said on Friday it was issuing 170 million preferred shares to raise T$4.25 billion for its expansion.
TI-Acer is a joint venture of Taiwan's Acer Inc, which holds 48 percent, and the U.S.-based Texas Instruments which has 33.34 percent. Other investors hold the rest.
The underwriting price was set at T$25 per share.

Of the 170 million shares, 120 million are for existing shareholders, while 50 million are offered to institutional investors as special bond-type shares, a type first issued by a Taiwanese company, venture spokeswoman Ruth Pao said.
"Since TI-Acer is not a listed company, we cannot issue corporate bonds, so we issue the special type of preferred shares to raise funds," Pao told Reuters by telephone.

While ordinary preferred shares carry a right to demand company dividend issues, the special shares have no such right. Instead, they can demand an annual interest rate of at least nine percent, which Pao likened to a bond yield.
"According to the contracts, TI-Acer must redeem the 50 million shares within three years," she said.
Proceeds will be used to finance the venture's US$1.35 billion eight-inch wafer fabrication plant, Pao said.
TI-Acer said in June it was slowing construction of the plant because of plunging prices for four- and 16-megabit dynamic random access memory chips.
"We will complete the contruction by the end of 1996, but equipment installation and formal production will be delayed to 1997 depending on demand conditions then," Pao said.

TI-Acer said in June that it was halting production of four-megabit DRAM chips because months of price-slashing had made it virtually unprofitable, and instead it was focussing on production of 16-megabit chips.
